use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

claims.content: The C2 JU initiates action—automatically or manually—to resolve the dual designation when it recognizes that two interface-reported tracks are eligible for correlation, or performs correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units.
The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
Upon acceptance of the requested correlation, the receiving IUs retain the designated Retained TN and drop the designated Dropped TN.
Upon successful correlation execution, if the own unit holds the Dropped TN as a local or common local track, the Retained TN is designated as a common local track.

Upon correlation execution, specific data fields from the Dropped TN are transferred to the Retained TN: Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, Altitude Source, TQ, and Strength (if the Dropped TN was a local or common local track).

Identification data transfer following correlation is governed by ID conflict restrictions: if restricted and IDs differ, the last Identity reported for the Dropped TN is processed as an Identity Difference Report for the Retained TN; otherwise, specific ID/IAD and platform attributes are transferred.
If the originating C2 JU (own unit) holds R2 for the Dropped TN, the Dropped TN is dropped and the J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted after the J7.2 message.
For a correlation executed under the J10.2 engagement-status exception, the Unknown/Hostile track is the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
After acceptance of a manual correlation (RV field set to value 3), the resulting track is not subject to automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
The goal of the use case is to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The goal of the use case is to resolve dual designations by correlating two tracks reported to the interface that are eligible for correlation.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: Two ballistic missile tracks reported on the interface are eligible for correlation, meaning they have successfully passed the second correlation test and have no correlation restriction; C2 JU correlates them, resolving the dual designation so that the reported track represents a single data point.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The instance starts when two ballistic missile tracks reported on the interface are eligible for correlation and require dual designation resolution.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
in_scope_actions: Process two ballistic missile tracks for dual designation resolution after they are eligible for correlation
Correlate the two eligible tracks reported on the interface
Resolve the dual designation so the reported track represents a single data point
excluded_adjacent_actions: Minimizing the general occurrence and duration of dual designations across the interface
Post-correlation track-data or identification-data transfer to the retained track
Drop-track messaging and downstream disposition of the dropped track

claims.content: On receipt of a J7.2 Correlation message, if the receiving C2 JU holds OCCs on both subject tracks, or holds conflicting IDs on the two tracks while the ID conflict correlation restriction is enabled, the JU shall reject the correlation and transmit a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.

If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction, the C2 JU shall alert the operator to either (a) change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation, or (b) transmit an ID Difference Report, thereby allowing automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
Manual correlation of two tracks shall not be performed if they are of a different E/C, or one is simulated and the other is live, or both are remote.

If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track; however, when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message is discarded.

If a ballistic missile track is lost because no local sensor data has been received since the last transmitted update or the JU determines the track is lost by other system criteria, subsequent reports include held data and set the Lost Track Indicator to value 1; a JU reporting Lost Track data is assumed to have a TQ of 5 less than the reported TQ, so a JU holding Tracking data may assume R2 with a TQ of 11 when the Lost Track report has a TQ of 15.
If it is determined that more than one data point exists for a ballistic missile track currently being reported, track decorrelation shall occur.

If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, automatic correlation may be allowed despite the correlation restriction.

Diverges from Step 2 (automatic initiation of correlation): the C2 JU may instead manually initiate correlation of any two tracks irrespective of the correlation test criteria in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f, the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g, or the requirements in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.

Diverges from Step 3 (correlation execution): instead of executing the requested Retained TN/Dropped TN assignment, the responding C2 JU may transmit a reverse correlation J7.2 message with the originally received Retained TN and Dropped TN reversed and the RV field set to value 1.

Diverges from Step 4 (correlation performance and acceptance) for a manually initiated correlation (RV=3): if the Retained TN is not held but the Dropped TN is held and has an OCC, the system executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.
The C2 JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface have successfully passed the second correlation test and have no correlation restriction, making them eligible for correlation.
The C2 JU initiates action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.

The recognizing C2 JU initiates transmission of the J7.2 Correlation message, which requests all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks and identifies the Retained TN and Dropped TN selected in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1j.

C² JUs perform correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units, and the receiving IUs accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow them to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
The dual designation is resolved via correlation; the reported ballistic missile track represents a single data point.
A TN pair has been determined to be a dual designation.

The two tracks reported on the interface are eligible for correlation: they have passed the required correlation tests and restrictions (including Course, Speed, and Altitude Differential), and the positions of all tracks and IUs tested are extrapolated to the same time.

Automatic correlation is not disqualified for the track pair because either: (a) local/remote data held do not indicate a conflicting Identity (ID) difference, neither track has a Strength field greater than 1 (unless set to No Statement), and the tracks do not have different Mode II codes while the local Mode II code is current; or (b) the J10.2 engagement-status exception applies — either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, the other subject track has an ID of Friend, and the Unknown/Hostile track is the Dropped TN — so automatic correlation may be allowed despite the ID-conflict and Mode II restrictions, and neither track has a Strength field greater than 1 (unless set to No Statement).
C2 JU

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger defines two alternative entries: (a) the C2 JU initiates correlation after recognizing eligibility, or (b) the C2 JU performs correlation tests in response to a correlation request from another unit. Main Flow step 1 only continues the self-initiated path by starting with the C2 JU recognizing eligibility; steps 2-3 then describe the self-initiated J7.2 transmission. A unit entering via the response-trigger branch would not begin by recognizing its own eligibility or by sending a J7.2; it would begin with receipt/processing of the incoming correlation request. Thus the response-trigger branch is not continued by the Main Flow. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit flow continuation to 'the next step' or to a separate step is not supported by the cited cards; the cards support the recognizing unit initiating action and the receiving unit performing correlation tests.))

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 2 says it diverges from 'Step 3 (correlation execution)', but main_flow Step 3 is the recognizing C2 JU's transmission of the J7.2 Correlation message, not the execution/correlation-response step. The responding C2 JU's reverse-correlation alternative belongs to Step 4, which governs receiving IUs' acceptance/rejection/reverse responses. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (Explicit evidence that this reverse correlation response occurs at Step 4 instead of accepting the requested Retained TN/Dropped TN assignment.; Explicit recovery/exit behavior after transmitting the reverse correlation J7.2 message.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The Main Flow ends at recognition/initiation, J7.2 transmission, acceptance by receiving IUs, and correlation resolution. It does not include the post-correlation transfer of track data/ID fields or the J7.0 Drop Track message transmission that appears in the postconditions, and the scope_contract explicitly lists post-correlation track-data/ID transfer and drop-track messaging as excluded_adjacent_actions. Thus those postconditions are not reachable commitments of this use case as written.

[altflow_diverge_points] Alternative flow claim 2 says it diverges from main_flow Step 3 ('correlation execution'), but main_flow Step 3 is the recognizing C2 JU's transmission of the J7.2 request. The reverse-correlation J7.2 response is a receiving/responding C2 JU action and is already described in main_flow Step 4, so the attachment point is logically unrelated.

inconsistency_hints: Preconditions claim 3 states unconditionally that no automatic-correlation restriction applies, but Postcondition 7 describes a valid automatic-correlation path despite an ID restriction (J10.2 engagement status with Unknown/Hostile vs Friend). The J10.2 exception is an external eligibility state that must be true before the trigger can initiate correlation in that path; it is missing from Preconditions.

The Trigger contains a second disjunct in which the C2 JU performs correlation tests in response to correlation requests from other units. Main Flow step 1 begins with the C2 JU recognizing already-eligible tracks and step 3 transmits a J7.2 request; the request-response path is never carried into Main Flow, so the Trigger cannot continue into this scenario.

The Trigger allows automatic or manual initiation, but Main Flow step 2 only initiates automatic action. As a result, the manual-correlation postcondition (RV=3, no automatic decorrelation for 5 minutes) is unreachable from the described Main Flow.

Alternative flow claim 3 also attaches to 'Step 3 (correlation execution)', but Step 3 is only the J7.2 message transmission/request. The manually initiated RV=3 ownership branch is an execution-time response by the system/responding C2 JU, so it should attach to Step 4, the step describing correlation performance and acceptance by receiving IUs.

Postcondition 7 restates the J10.2 engagement-status exception from Precondition 3(b) as a permissive condition: 'automatic correlation may be allowed despite the restriction.' That is an eligibility condition upstream of the Main Flow, not a state produced by the Main Flow. The Main Flow can resolve the dual designation, but it cannot lead to the permissibility of automatic correlation; the exception enables the flow rather than being reached by it.
